messages:
alex: CI artifact publish failed for CI#12456 when pushing redwood-llm-serve:v2.3.1 to registry.redwood-inference.internal. saw: 'manifest put failed: manifest invalid: blob unknown to registry'. build used a recent Dockerfile refactor (squash + new multistage). can someone quick-check?
infra-bot: :warning: CI#12456: publish step failed (push step) — job link: https://ci.redwood/12456 — exit code 1
sam: reassigning to @tina who touched the Dockerfile. did the base image change layers?
tina: looking now. i saw a couple of weird cache misses on local; pushing manually to the registry gave a 401 once then succeeded on retry. might be transient token flap. logs from push:```
# push snippet
Pushing manifest for digest sha256:abcd1234...
PUT /v2/redwood/llm/manifest
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"errors":[{"code":"MANIFEST_INVALID","message":"blob unknown to registry"}]}
```

pj: hmm could be two simultaneous builds reusing the same temp tag and one GC-ed a layer. CI uses parallel workers and the refactor changed layer ordering. can we check buildkit settings and whether we enabled --squash?

alex: CI step used DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 and moby buildkit, with cache-from referencing previous image tag. Dockerfile added an additional 'pip install --no-cache' layer near the end. i suspect cache-from gave a stale layer ID mapping.

sam: quick triage plan: 1) try a single controlled rerun on the failing commit without cache (CI var NO_CACHE=1) 2) if it repros, request a bisect across the last two Dockerfile commits to find which change reordered layers 3) check registry bucket logs for deleted blob events around the push timestamp
tina: running a manual local build with --no-cache now, will attempt push to the staging registry and report.

infra-bot: triggered rerun: CI#12456-rerun-1 by tina

pj: also verify auth tokens for the CI runner. the 401 on manual retry is worrying — could be token rotation between build and push (we rotate ephemeral creds every 10m). add a short sleep before push or refresh token right before push step as a quick mitigation.

alex: good call. i'll add a small token-refresh step and set NO_CACHE=1 for the rerun. also adding explicit image tags per stage (avoid ephemeral stage tags that might collide).

sam: if rerun passes, we should still run a quick canary where we build with cache, push, and then pull the image on a different worker to ensure manifest integrity.

tina: manual rerun done: local build (no-cache) pushed to staging successfully. CI rerun is in progress.

infra-bot: CI#12456-rerun-1: job succeeded (publish to staging)

alex: CI rerun passed with NO_CACHE and token refresh. leaving original failure open for postmortem but we can hotfix by disabling cache-from until we confirm stable behavior.

pj: for postmortem items: 1) add registry audit for blob deletions 2) make CI refresh ephemeral creds immediately before push 3) avoid cache-from on multi-stage refactors for two weeks 4) add a short retry/backoff on manifest push when registry returns MANIFEST_INVALID

sam: filing a small ticket: ENGINFRA-4122 with the actions above. tagging @product to know deploy may be delayed by a day. :clipboard:
alex: thanks everyone. closing this triage thread — will follow up in ENGINFRA-4122 with logs and timeline. :thumbsup:
